Wave 21 — Run-secrets grow a tenant wall: per-workspace scoping (D9), designed then built

content.value: Survey (12 coverage-accounted reports) is folded in below. A 5-verifier fleet is in flight: 2 Opus (live migration/PK probe in a worktree; PK-fork necessity ruling) + 3 Sonnet (CI gate + collisions, ledger/prior-art, FK + audit shape). Next: Decide ratifies D191+ and cuts slices; builders implement.

Ratify + build RUN-SECRETS PER-WORKSPACE SCOPING (task-5766dc5ca985ddc8), the D9 premise correction. Today's run-secrets store is FLAT INSTANCE-GLOBAL: table `secrets` with PK :name, columns value/updated_at/updated_by, zero tenant column; Barkpark.Secrets.get/put/reveal/delete key only on name; list/0 returns every secret in the instance; /v1/secrets/* is gated flat :require_admin. This blocks knob-4 (grant-scoped per-workspace token mint, D24) and true per-workspace credential isolation in the Cloud runner. Wave shape: (A) RATIFY the scoping design as a real charter decision D191+, grounded in the actual code + docs/contracts/tenancy.md + the chat_sessions owner_workspace_id prior art, naming the failure mode each choice prevents; (B) BUILD it — schema change + safe migration + scoped read/write + a RED-FIRST protective test proving cross-workspace isolation (must red on today's flat-global code). All offline Elixir, rides elixir.yml. Scope tightly: one coherent capability, 2-3 disjoint slices; knob-4 only if honestly small, else a now-unblocked follow-up.

Confirmed against origin/main: api/lib/barkpark/secrets.ex + secrets/secret_record.ex are exactly as D9 recorded — @primary_key {:name, :string}, no workspace_id anywhere, Repo.get(SecretRecord, name) on every path, list/0 unfiltered. The D9 premise stands; no contradiction found. One crucial wrinkle the design MUST honor: ingest_token/0 is a legitimate INSTANCE-GLOBAL consumer (DB-first, env-fallback resolver for the cloud ingest shared secret) — a hard tenant seal that abolishes global secrets would break it. The store therefore needs TWO tiers, not a blanket migration of every row into a workspace.

The finished experience: a workspace's secrets live inside its tenant wall. Workspace A's admin can put/get/list/reveal/delete A's secrets and can NEVER see that B's secrets even exist; a nil or undecidable workspace resolves to ZERO rows (fail-closed, the scope_to_workspace/3 law); instance-global system secrets (ingest token) keep working untouched on an EXPLICITLY-global path that no workspace-scoped call can reach by accident. The knob-4 token mint can then read its per-workspace material without an admin token — the exact anti-pattern D37 called out dies here.

items.value: Tentative lean 1 — ADDITIVE nullable workspace column, not a PK rewrite of doom. Add workspace_id (:binary_id, nullable) to secrets; NULL = instance-global system secret. Replace PK-on-name uniqueness with two partial unique indexes: UNIQUE(name) WHERE workspace_id IS NULL and UNIQUE(workspace_id, name) WHERE workspace_id IS NOT NULL. Failure mode prevented: a destructive PK migration that could drop or collide existing prod secrets (migrations are irreversible-sensitive; nullable-add + no backfill = zero-risk).

Tentative lean 2 — TWO EXPLICIT TIERS, no silent fallback. Scoped reads (get/list/reveal with workspace_id) see ONLY that workspace's rows — a NULL-owner global secret is INVISIBLE to the scoped path, and a foreign workspace's row is invisible. The legacy get/1 global path reads ONLY WHERE workspace_id IS NULL. Failure modes prevented: (a) instance credentials leaking to tenants via fallback-to-global reads; (b) a tenant secret shadowing a system secret name; (c) the D35-class NULL-owner leak where global callers read everything.

Tentative lean 3 — fail-closed on nil. A scoped call with nil/invalid workspace_id compiles to zero rows or raises — never falls through to the global tier (mirror scope_to_workspace/3's where:false law).

Tentative lean 4 — migration = nullable add + indexes ONLY; existing rows stay NULL (they ARE instance-global today — backfilling them into a workspace would be inventing tenancy that never existed). No dual-read bridge needed because the tiers are disjoint by definition.

Tentative lean 5 — keep Cloak EncryptedBinary for at-rest encryption THIS wave; the W6 per-workspace DEK envelope question (does a row-swap attack matter when the value column carries no AAD binding to workspace_id?) gets a survey + verify answer and, if real, a NAMED residual-risk note or a small AAD follow-up — not silent scope creep.
Tentative lean 6 — audit rows (SecretAudit) gain the workspace dimension so a reveal in workspace A is attributable to A.

Tentative lean 7 — slices: S1 schema+migration+scoped context functions+red-first isolation test (the core, must land); S2 HTTP/admin surface scoping IF it lands without touching router.ex (survey decides; router.ex is off-limits this wave); S3 knob-4 consumer ONLY if honestly small — else file it as the now-unblocked follow-up.

blocks.text: Survey digest — what 12 scouts established (Digest phase, 2026-07-17)

content.value: D9 is confirmed at every layer, live on origin/main: secrets is a flat instance-global encrypted KV. The name column is the LITERAL Postgres primary key (migration 20260629140000: add :name, :string, primary_key: true), every context function keys on bare name (get:29, reveal:42, put:68, list:98 unfiltered, delete:112), /v1/secrets is gated flat [:api, :require_admin] with zero workspace resolution, and secrets_audit has no workspace dimension either. Exactly TWO production callers exist repo-wide: SecretController (admin HTTP CRUD via list/reveal/put/delete — never get/1) and RequireIngestToken -> ingest_token/0, the SOLE caller of get/1 and a structurally instance-global consumer (the bearer check runs before any workspace is resolvable). Consequence: making get/1 global-tier-only (WHERE workspace_id IS NULL) breaks nothing.

Prior art is nailed and directly crib-able: the chat_sessions owner_workspace_id seam (migration 20260713140000: nullable :binary_id, NO FK, no default, no backfill, partial composite index) + studio_chat.ex scope_sessions/2 — a 3-clause fail-closed gate (:global passthrough / binary equality / anything-else -> where(false)) — plus the red-first isolation test template at studio_chat_test.exs:2298-2431, including the critical sub-case: a NULL-owner global row is INVISIBLE to ANY workspace scope, no is_nil OR-carveout. Content.Scope.scope_to_workspace/3 (content/scope.ex:111-127) and docs/contracts/tenancy.md:52 state the same fail-closed law. Test harness: TenancyFixtures.create_workspace! + the content_get_document_tenant_isolation_test.exs sanity-then-leak-guard structure; a secrets-specific direct-insert fixture must be built alongside (none exists).

Lean 1 said 'additive nullable column, NOT a PK rewrite'. The migration-shape scout proved that is only half-available: Postgres PRIMARY KEYs cannot be partial, so as long as name stays the PK, workspace A and workspace B can NEVER both own a secret named openai_api_key — which defeats the point of tenant scoping. The clean path (mirroring every other tenant-scoped table, all born with surrogate PKs): add surrogate id :binary_id PK, DROP CONSTRAINT secrets_pkey (data-nondestructive — no row or value touched), demote name to a plain NOT NULL column, then the two partial unique indexes. Blast radius: 4 Repo.get(SecretRecord, name) call sites become Repo.get_by, and — unsurveyed subtlety — put/3's upsert (on_conflict conflict_target: :name) BREAKS against partial unique indexes and needs a new conflict-target form. There is NO DROP CONSTRAINT precedent anywhere in the migration history. Verify assignment V1 proves the whole mechanism live before D191 ratifies it; V2 rules on whether per-workspace name reuse is genuinely required (charter + credential_ref semantics say yes, but the ruling must be explicit).

items.value: W6 DEK envelope: NOT reusable — it is connectors/src/crypto/credential-cipher.ts, Node-only, HKDF per-call, deliberately walled off by charter D38 ('no Elixir will ever decrypt one'). The Elixir-native analog, if crypto-binding is ever wanted, is Crypto.DataKeys + FieldCipher (scope-as-AAD, D51-D54). Lean 5 (keep Cloak EncryptedBinary this wave) stands.

NEW security finding (not previously in the charter): Cloak's AES-GCM AAD is the hardcoded constant "AES256GCM" (deps/cloak aes_gcm.ex:12) — a ciphertext blob copied between rows decrypts cleanly. The W21 tenant wall is SQL-enforced ONLY, never cryptographic. D191 must name this as a residual risk and file the FieldCipher/DataKeys upgrade as an explicit follow-up task — no silent claim of crypto isolation.

S2 (scoped admin HTTP surface) genuinely requires router.ex lines — the proven :scoped_admin pattern (schemas/webhooks/token-mint, router.ex:2157-2213) needs a new scope block, and router.ex is off-limits this wave. SecretController stays flat-global on the new schema; DANGER noted: the :api pipeline's AssignDefaultScope stamps current_workspace=Default, so the controller must keep calling the GLOBAL tier explicitly, never accidentally scope legacy writes to 'Default'. S2 + the manifest auth_tier flip (bp secret * currently blanket 'admin' in capabilities.ex ~1416-1463) become one named follow-up.

Knob-4 is NOT a small S3: no grant object exists anywhere (connector_installs has zero permission/scope fields; the mint is hardcoded ~w(read write), auth.ex:678), and W15/D148 already declined the policy half — 'building it would manufacture a fake correlation'. Follow-up filed with the honest amendment: D9 scoping is necessary but NOT sufficient; knob-4 also needs a grant-model design decision.

No consumer exists today: the Cloud runner deliberately bypasses Barkpark.Secrets (D23/D110 — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from ambient env only). A scoped store lands consumer-less; the wave must say so honestly and file 'wire the first scoped consumer' as a follow-up rather than imply the runner reads it.

plugin_settings is the same flat shape but a legitimately instance-global sibling (singleton GitHub App / Bokbasen / Indx config) — EXPLICITLY out of scope, named exclusion with a forward pointer, not a leak.

No naming-convention hack exists (no workspace-prefixed names anywhere); no Studio LiveView renders secrets (nothing to seal there); CLI bp secret * is manifest-driven so sealing HTTP seals the CLI for free.

blocks.text: Decisions D191–D198 (charter is the memory; one line each)

items.value: D191 — Surrogate-PK two-tier schema: drop secrets_pkey, id binary_id PK (gen_random_uuid backfill), nullable workspace_id, two partial unique indexes (global arm byte-identical to today's uniqueness; workspace arm permits per-tenant name reuse). Why: the PK-total fact + the enumeration oracle; every mechanic run-proven.

D192 — FK to workspaces, on_delete: :delete_all, on secrets AND secrets_audit. Why: data_keys/E1 majority law; an orphaned encrypted credential is a forgotten-secret surface; isolation itself is FK-independent. Tests must use real TenancyFixtures workspaces.

D193 — Scope-arg threading (studio_chat scope_sessions precedent), default :global = explicit NULL-tier arm (never all-rows); binary = equality; else fail-closed zero rows. No cross-tier visibility in either direction; get/1 stays global-pinned (sole caller ingest_token/0).

D194 — The three upsert/changeset corrections: tier-branched unsafe_fragment conflict_target; on_conflict narrowed to {:replace,[:value,:updated_at,:updated_by]}; BOTH named unique_constraints declared. All run-proven; 409-not-500 is the difference.
D195 — secrets_audit gains workspace_id + [workspace_id,inserted_at] index; action vocab (set/reveal/delete) unchanged.

D196 — Named residuals/exclusions: (a) the wall is SQL-only — Cloak AAD is the hardcoded "AES256GCM" constant; AAD upgrade filed as connectors-secrets-aad-binding. (b) W6 DEK is Node-only, D38-walled — closed door. (c) plugin_settings stays instance-global by design. (d) no scoped consumer exists — filed as connectors-secrets-first-scoped-consumer.

D197 — S2 (scoped-admin HTTP + bp secret.* manifest auth_tier) is a follow-up: the proven pattern needs new router.ex lines (off-limits this wave); in-controller workaround declined. Filed connectors-secrets-scoped-admin-http; the core task's criterion 1 amended accordingly.
D198 — Knob-4 wording law: D9 is necessary-but-not-sufficient; cite D148, never D125; no new knob-4 task (would duplicate fe78ccb crit-2 + connectors-cloud-credential-config-embed).

content.value: One slice, reviewed as the last hands before merge in a fresh worktree branched off the built commit (deea1129b). The gate re-ran GREEN on the reviewer's final state — 31 tests, 0 failures (12 secrets_test back-compat + 10 isolation + 9 secret_controller) on a dedicated partition DB that auto-created and migrated the surrogate-PK schema cleanly. mix format --check-formatted passes on all five changed files. The reviewer changed nothing, so the final branch is the builder's original.

Run-secrets are no longer flat instance-global. The store now carries a two-tier identity (NULL workspace_id = instance-global, non-NULL = one workspace) behind a fail-closed scope gate that mirrors StudioChat.scope_sessions/2. Workspace A cannot read, reveal, list, or delete workspace B's secret; instance globals never leak into a tenant scope and tenant rows never shadow ingest_token; a nil/invalid scope reads zero rows and refuses writes with {:error, :invalid_scope}. The wall is SQL-only, not cryptographic (Cloak's AAD is a constant) — a named, filed residual (connectors-secrets-aad-binding), not a silent gap.

Wave 21 — Run-secrets grow a tenant wall: per-workspace scoping (D9), designed then built

content.value: Survey (12 coverage-accounted reports) is folded in below. A 5-verifier fleet is in flight: 2 Opus (live migration/PK probe in a worktree; PK-fork necessity ruling) + 3 Sonnet (CI gate + collisions, ledger/prior-art, FK + audit shape). Next: Decide ratifies D191+ and cuts slices; builders implement.

Ratify + build RUN-SECRETS PER-WORKSPACE SCOPING (task-5766dc5ca985ddc8), the D9 premise correction. Today's run-secrets store is FLAT INSTANCE-GLOBAL: table `secrets` with PK :name, columns value/updated_at/updated_by, zero tenant column; Barkpark.Secrets.get/put/reveal/delete key only on name; list/0 returns every secret in the instance; /v1/secrets/* is gated flat :require_admin. This blocks knob-4 (grant-scoped per-workspace token mint, D24) and true per-workspace credential isolation in the Cloud runner. Wave shape: (A) RATIFY the scoping design as a real charter decision D191+, grounded in the actual code + docs/contracts/tenancy.md + the chat_sessions owner_workspace_id prior art, naming the failure mode each choice prevents; (B) BUILD it — schema change + safe migration + scoped read/write + a RED-FIRST protective test proving cross-workspace isolation (must red on today's flat-global code). All offline Elixir, rides elixir.yml. Scope tightly: one coherent capability, 2-3 disjoint slices; knob-4 only if honestly small, else a now-unblocked follow-up.

Confirmed against origin/main: api/lib/barkpark/secrets.ex + secrets/secret_record.ex are exactly as D9 recorded — @primary_key {:name, :string}, no workspace_id anywhere, Repo.get(SecretRecord, name) on every path, list/0 unfiltered. The D9 premise stands; no contradiction found. One crucial wrinkle the design MUST honor: ingest_token/0 is a legitimate INSTANCE-GLOBAL consumer (DB-first, env-fallback resolver for the cloud ingest shared secret) — a hard tenant seal that abolishes global secrets would break it. The store therefore needs TWO tiers, not a blanket migration of every row into a workspace.

The finished experience: a workspace's secrets live inside its tenant wall. Workspace A's admin can put/get/list/reveal/delete A's secrets and can NEVER see that B's secrets even exist; a nil or undecidable workspace resolves to ZERO rows (fail-closed, the scope_to_workspace/3 law); instance-global system secrets (ingest token) keep working untouched on an EXPLICITLY-global path that no workspace-scoped call can reach by accident. The knob-4 token mint can then read its per-workspace material without an admin token — the exact anti-pattern D37 called out dies here.

items.value: Tentative lean 1 — ADDITIVE nullable workspace column, not a PK rewrite of doom. Add workspace_id (:binary_id, nullable) to secrets; NULL = instance-global system secret. Replace PK-on-name uniqueness with two partial unique indexes: UNIQUE(name) WHERE workspace_id IS NULL and UNIQUE(workspace_id, name) WHERE workspace_id IS NOT NULL. Failure mode prevented: a destructive PK migration that could drop or collide existing prod secrets (migrations are irreversible-sensitive; nullable-add + no backfill = zero-risk).

Tentative lean 2 — TWO EXPLICIT TIERS, no silent fallback. Scoped reads (get/list/reveal with workspace_id) see ONLY that workspace's rows — a NULL-owner global secret is INVISIBLE to the scoped path, and a foreign workspace's row is invisible. The legacy get/1 global path reads ONLY WHERE workspace_id IS NULL. Failure modes prevented: (a) instance credentials leaking to tenants via fallback-to-global reads; (b) a tenant secret shadowing a system secret name; (c) the D35-class NULL-owner leak where global callers read everything.

Tentative lean 3 — fail-closed on nil. A scoped call with nil/invalid workspace_id compiles to zero rows or raises — never falls through to the global tier (mirror scope_to_workspace/3's where:false law).

Tentative lean 4 — migration = nullable add + indexes ONLY; existing rows stay NULL (they ARE instance-global today — backfilling them into a workspace would be inventing tenancy that never existed). No dual-read bridge needed because the tiers are disjoint by definition.

Tentative lean 5 — keep Cloak EncryptedBinary for at-rest encryption THIS wave; the W6 per-workspace DEK envelope question (does a row-swap attack matter when the value column carries no AAD binding to workspace_id?) gets a survey + verify answer and, if real, a NAMED residual-risk note or a small AAD follow-up — not silent scope creep.
Tentative lean 6 — audit rows (SecretAudit) gain the workspace dimension so a reveal in workspace A is attributable to A.

Tentative lean 7 — slices: S1 schema+migration+scoped context functions+red-first isolation test (the core, must land); S2 HTTP/admin surface scoping IF it lands without touching router.ex (survey decides; router.ex is off-limits this wave); S3 knob-4 consumer ONLY if honestly small — else file it as the now-unblocked follow-up.

blocks.text: Survey digest — what 12 scouts established (Digest phase, 2026-07-17)

content.value: D9 is confirmed at every layer, live on origin/main: secrets is a flat instance-global encrypted KV. The name column is the LITERAL Postgres primary key (migration 20260629140000: add :name, :string, primary_key: true), every context function keys on bare name (get:29, reveal:42, put:68, list:98 unfiltered, delete:112), /v1/secrets is gated flat [:api, :require_admin] with zero workspace resolution, and secrets_audit has no workspace dimension either. Exactly TWO production callers exist repo-wide: SecretController (admin HTTP CRUD via list/reveal/put/delete — never get/1) and RequireIngestToken -> ingest_token/0, the SOLE caller of get/1 and a structurally instance-global consumer (the bearer check runs before any workspace is resolvable). Consequence: making get/1 global-tier-only (WHERE workspace_id IS NULL) breaks nothing.

Prior art is nailed and directly crib-able: the chat_sessions owner_workspace_id seam (migration 20260713140000: nullable :binary_id, NO FK, no default, no backfill, partial composite index) + studio_chat.ex scope_sessions/2 — a 3-clause fail-closed gate (:global passthrough / binary equality / anything-else -> where(false)) — plus the red-first isolation test template at studio_chat_test.exs:2298-2431, including the critical sub-case: a NULL-owner global row is INVISIBLE to ANY workspace scope, no is_nil OR-carveout. Content.Scope.scope_to_workspace/3 (content/scope.ex:111-127) and docs/contracts/tenancy.md:52 state the same fail-closed law. Test harness: TenancyFixtures.create_workspace! + the content_get_document_tenant_isolation_test.exs sanity-then-leak-guard structure; a secrets-specific direct-insert fixture must be built alongside (none exists).

Lean 1 said 'additive nullable column, NOT a PK rewrite'. The migration-shape scout proved that is only half-available: Postgres PRIMARY KEYs cannot be partial, so as long as name stays the PK, workspace A and workspace B can NEVER both own a secret named openai_api_key — which defeats the point of tenant scoping. The clean path (mirroring every other tenant-scoped table, all born with surrogate PKs): add surrogate id :binary_id PK, DROP CONSTRAINT secrets_pkey (data-nondestructive — no row or value touched), demote name to a plain NOT NULL column, then the two partial unique indexes. Blast radius: 4 Repo.get(SecretRecord, name) call sites become Repo.get_by, and — unsurveyed subtlety — put/3's upsert (on_conflict conflict_target: :name) BREAKS against partial unique indexes and needs a new conflict-target form. There is NO DROP CONSTRAINT precedent anywhere in the migration history. Verify assignment V1 proves the whole mechanism live before D191 ratifies it; V2 rules on whether per-workspace name reuse is genuinely required (charter + credential_ref semantics say yes, but the ruling must be explicit).

items.value: W6 DEK envelope: NOT reusable — it is connectors/src/crypto/credential-cipher.ts, Node-only, HKDF per-call, deliberately walled off by charter D38 ('no Elixir will ever decrypt one'). NEW security finding (not previously in the charter): Cloak's AES-GCM AAD is the hardcoded constant "AES256GCM" (deps/cloak aes_gcm.ex:12) — a ciphertext blob copied between rows decrypts cleanly. The W21 tenant wall is SQL-enforced ONLY, never cryptographic. D191 must name this as a residual risk and file the FieldCipher/DataKeys upgrade as an explicit follow-up task — no silent claim of crypto isolation.

S2 (scoped admin HTTP surface) genuinely requires router.ex lines — the proven :scoped_admin pattern (schemas/webhooks/token-mint, router.ex:2157-2213) needs a new scope block, and router.ex is off-limits this wave. SecretController stays flat-global on the new schema; DANGER noted: the :api pipeline's AssignDefaultScope stamps current_workspace=Default, so the controller must keep calling the GLOBAL tier explicitly, never accidentally scope legacy writes to 'Default'. S2 + the manifest auth_tier flip (bp secret * currently blanket 'admin' in capabilities.ex ~1416-1463) become one named follow-up.

Knob-4 is NOT a small S3: no grant object exists anywhere (connector_installs has zero permission/scope fields; the mint is hardcoded ~w(read write), auth.ex:678), and W15/D148 already declined the policy half — 'building it would manufacture a fake correlation'. Follow-up filed with the honest amendment: D9 scoping is necessary but NOT sufficient; knob-4 also needs a grant-model design decision.

No consumer exists today: the Cloud runner deliberately bypasses Barkpark.Secrets (D23/D110 — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from ambient env only). A scoped store lands consumer-less; the wave must say so honestly and file 'wire the first scoped consumer' as a follow-up rather than imply the runner reads it.

blocks.text: Decisions D191–D198 (charter is the memory; one line each)

items.value: D191 — Surrogate-PK two-tier schema: drop secrets_pkey, id binary_id PK (gen_random_uuid backfill), nullable workspace_id, two partial unique indexes (global arm byte-identical to today's uniqueness; workspace arm permits per-tenant name reuse). CONNECTORS EPIC · WAVE 21 · DESIGN WAVE · STRATEGIZE · 2026-07-17

Wave 21 — Run-secrets grow a tenant wall: per-workspace scoping (D9), designed then built

IN FLIGHT — verifying
Survey (12 coverage-accounted reports) is folded in below. A 5-verifier fleet is in flight: 2 Opus (live migration/PK probe in a worktree; PK-fork necessity ruling) + 3 Sonnet (CI gate + collisions, ledger/prior-art, FK + audit shape). Next: Decide ratifies D191+ and cuts slices; builders implement.

The wish

Ratify + build RUN-SECRETS PER-WORKSPACE SCOPING (task-5766dc5ca985ddc8), the D9 premise correction. Today's run-secrets store is FLAT INSTANCE-GLOBAL: table `secrets` with PK :name, columns value/updated_at/updated_by, zero tenant column; Barkpark.Secrets.get/put/reveal/delete key only on name; list/0 returns every secret in the instance; /v1/secrets/* is gated flat :require_admin. This blocks knob-4 (grant-scoped per-workspace token mint, D24) and true per-workspace credential isolation in the Cloud runner. Wave shape: (A) RATIFY the scoping design as a real charter decision D191+, grounded in the actual code + docs/contracts/tenancy.md + the chat_sessions owner_workspace_id prior art, naming the failure mode each choice prevents; (B) BUILD it — schema change + safe migration + scoped read/write + a RED-FIRST protective test proving cross-workspace isolation (must red on today's flat-global code). All offline Elixir, rides elixir.yml. Scope tightly: one coherent capability, 2-3 disjoint slices; knob-4 only if honestly small, else a now-unblocked follow-up.

Premise check (done at Strategize)

Confirmed against origin/main: api/lib/barkpark/secrets.ex + secrets/secret_record.ex are exactly as D9 recorded — @primary_key {:name, :string}, no workspace_id anywhere, Repo.get(SecretRecord, name) on every path, list/0 unfiltered. The D9 premise stands; no contradiction found. One crucial wrinkle the design MUST honor: ingest_token/0 is a legitimate INSTANCE-GLOBAL consumer (DB-first, env-fallback resolver for the cloud ingest shared secret) — a hard tenant seal that abolishes global secrets would break it. The store therefore needs TWO tiers, not a blanket migration of every row into a workspace.

Strategic direction

The finished experience: a workspace's secrets live inside its tenant wall. Workspace A's admin can put/get/list/reveal/delete A's secrets and can NEVER see that B's secrets even exist; a nil or undecidable workspace resolves to ZERO rows (fail-closed, the scope_to_workspace/3 law); instance-global system secrets (ingest token) keep working untouched on an EXPLICITLY-global path that no workspace-scoped call can reach by accident. The knob-4 token mint can then read its per-workspace material without an admin token — the exact anti-pattern D37 called out dies here.

• Tentative lean 1 — ADDITIVE nullable workspace column, not a PK rewrite of doom. Add workspace_id (:binary_id, nullable) to secrets; NULL = instance-global system secret. Replace PK-on-name uniqueness with two partial unique indexes: UNIQUE(name) WHERE workspace_id IS NULL and UNIQUE(workspace_id, name) WHERE workspace_id IS NOT NULL. Failure mode prevented: a destructive PK migration that could drop or collide existing prod secrets (migrations are irreversible-sensitive; nullable-add + no backfill = zero-risk).
• Tentative lean 2 — TWO EXPLICIT TIERS, no silent fallback. Scoped reads (get/list/reveal with workspace_id) see ONLY that workspace's rows — a NULL-owner global secret is INVISIBLE to the scoped path, and a foreign workspace's row is invisible. The legacy get/1 global path reads ONLY WHERE workspace_id IS NULL. Failure modes prevented: (a) instance credentials leaking to tenants via fallback-to-global reads; (b) a tenant secret shadowing a system secret name; (c) the D35-class NULL-owner leak where global callers read everything.
• Tentative lean 3 — fail-closed on nil. A scoped call with nil/invalid workspace_id compiles to zero rows or raises — never falls through to the global tier (mirror scope_to_workspace/3's where:false law).
• Tentative lean 4 — migration = nullable add + indexes ONLY; existing rows stay NULL (they ARE instance-global today — backfilling them into a workspace would be inventing tenancy that never existed). No dual-read bridge needed because the tiers are disjoint by definition.
• Tentative lean 5 — keep Cloak EncryptedBinary for at-rest encryption THIS wave; the W6 per-workspace DEK envelope question (does a row-swap attack matter when the value column carries no AAD binding to workspace_id?) gets a survey + verify answer and, if real, a NAMED residual-risk note or a small AAD follow-up — not silent scope creep.
• Tentative lean 6 — audit rows (SecretAudit) gain the workspace dimension so a reveal in workspace A is attributable to A.
• Tentative lean 7 — slices: S1 schema+migration+scoped context functions+red-first isolation test (the core, must land); S2 HTTP/admin surface scoping IF it lands without touching router.ex (survey decides; router.ex is off-limits this wave); S3 knob-4 consumer ONLY if honestly small — else file it as the now-unblocked follow-up.

Quality bar: the isolation test MUST red on today's flat-global code before the fix greens it (distrust vacuous green). Column naming follows the repo's own vocabulary — survey decides between workspace_id (tenancy tables) and owner_workspace_id (chat_sessions P0 pattern). Do NOT overreach into the other design gates; keep production diffs minimal.

Survey plan — 14 scouts

1. secrets-impl-map — Full map of Barkpark.Secrets + SecretRecord + SecretAudit + EncryptedBinary: every public function, changesets, audit shape, the ingest_token resolver. WHY: The design patches THIS code; the ratified D191 must name real functions, not imagined ones.
2. secrets-consumers — Every caller of Barkpark.Secrets.* across lib/ + cloud/ + internal/: which are legitimately instance-global vs which should be workspace-scoped? WHY: Decides NULL-owner semantics and whether any caller breaks when get/1 becomes global-tier-only.
3. secrets-http-surface — The /v1/secrets controller + pipeline: how is it gated, does workspace resolution already ride the plug chain, can scoped gating land WITHOUT touching router.ex? WHY: Determines whether slice S2 is in-scope this wave or a follow-up.
4. tenancy-scope-prior-art — scope_to_workspace/3 in content/scope.ex + the chat_sessions owner_workspace_id P0 slice: exact column shape (nullable? FK? default?), migration text, how the isolation tests were written red-first. WHY: The ratified design copies a proven pattern instead of inventing one.
5. dek-envelope-w6 — The per-workspace DEK envelope shipped for connector-install credentials (W6): where does it live, what API, does run-secrets reuse it cheaply or is Cloak EncryptedBinary the honest answer this wave? WHY: Settles lean 5 — reuse vs keep, with cost named.
6. encrypted-binary-aad — Does Cloak/EncryptedBinary bind any AAD/context? Can a ciphertext row be re-pointed to another workspace row (swap attack)? Compare FieldCipher's scope-is-the-AAD scheme. WHY: Names the residual risk or upgrades it to a slice.
7. migration-shape — Current secrets table DDL (original migration) + latest migration timestamps on origin/main; feasibility of nullable-add + partial unique indexes vs composite-PK rewrite; Postgres NULL-uniqueness behavior. WHY: The migration must be safe and collision-free; PK :name is the invasive bit to design around.
8. plugin-settings-sibling — Plugins.Settings (the sibling encrypted-KV): same flat shape? Does this wave's design need to cover it or explicitly exclude it? WHY: Prevents scope creep AND prevents a second flat store from becoming the new leak.
9. knob4-consumer — The D24 knob-4 grant-scoped token mint: where would it consume workspace secrets, what exists already (Auth.create_token/5, chat_token_controller), is it honestly small once scoping lands? WHY: Decides whether S3 rides this wave or gets filed as the unblocked follow-up.
10. cloud-runner-reads — How the Cloud runner / assignment runtime reads run-secrets today (env injection? resolver poll?) and which of those reads must become workspace-scoped. WHY: The scoped read path must serve the actual runner consumer, not a hypothetical one.
11. test-harness — Existing secrets tests + DataCase multi-workspace fixture patterns (create_workspace_with_owner): where does the red-first isolation test live and what fixtures does it need? WHY: Builders get a paved test path; the red-first bar is non-negotiable.
12. naming-convention-hack — Does ANY code already write workspace-prefixed secret names (e.g. slack_bot_token:<ws>) as a scoping hack? WHY: A convention-hack row would need migration accommodation or explicit kill.
13. charter-decision-state — The charter's current highest D number + every decision touching secrets (D9, D24, D37) + any open/foreign ledger tasks referencing run-secrets. WHY: D191+ must not collide or contradict; avoids duplicate work with concurrent sessions.
14. audit-and-list-surface — Who reads SecretAudit and Secrets.list/0 (Studio? CLI? admin UI?): every surface that renders the secret list and would need the workspace filter. WHY: list/0 is the loudest leak (every tenant's secret NAMES); all its consumers must be sealed together.

Ledger

Epic: bp-connectors-epic (task-e640bb01fca6ea38). Driving task: task-5766dc5ca985ddc8 (run-secrets per-workspace scoping, P1, D9 correction). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-connectors-charter.md — this wave ratifies D191+ at Decide. Merge discipline: integration branch loop-epic/connectors-w21-integration, builders branch off origin/main, elixir.yml gate, targeted test runs only, PRs carry a Task: <slug> line per slice.

Survey digest — what 12 scouts established (Digest phase, 2026-07-17)

D9 is confirmed at every layer, live on origin/main: secrets is a flat instance-global encrypted KV. The name column is the LITERAL Postgres primary key (migration 20260629140000: add :name, :string, primary_key: true), every context function keys on bare name (get:29, reveal:42, put:68, list:98 unfiltered, delete:112), /v1/secrets is gated flat [:api, :require_admin] with zero workspace resolution, and secrets_audit has no workspace dimension either. Exactly TWO production callers exist repo-wide: SecretController (admin HTTP CRUD via list/reveal/put/delete — never get/1) and RequireIngestToken -> ingest_token/0, the SOLE caller of get/1 and a structurally instance-global consumer (the bearer check runs before any workspace is resolvable). Consequence: making get/1 global-tier-only (WHERE workspace_id IS NULL) breaks nothing.

Prior art is nailed and directly crib-able: the chat_sessions owner_workspace_id seam (migration 20260713140000: nullable :binary_id, NO FK, no default, no backfill, partial composite index) + studio_chat.ex scope_sessions/2 — a 3-clause fail-closed gate (:global passthrough / binary equality / anything-else -> where(false)) — plus the red-first isolation test template at studio_chat_test.exs:2298-2431, including the critical sub-case: a NULL-owner global row is INVISIBLE to ANY workspace scope, no is_nil OR-carveout. Content.Scope.scope_to_workspace/3 (content/scope.ex:111-127) and docs/contracts/tenancy.md:52 state the same fail-closed law. Test harness: TenancyFixtures.create_workspace! + the content_get_document_tenant_isolation_test.exs sanity-then-leak-guard structure; a secrets-specific direct-insert fixture must be built alongside (none exists).

CONTRADICTION with the strategic direction — the PK cannot silently survive
Lean 1 said 'additive nullable column, NOT a PK rewrite'. The migration-shape scout proved that is only half-available: Postgres PRIMARY KEYs cannot be partial, so as long as name stays the PK, workspace A and workspace B can NEVER both own a secret named openai_api_key — which defeats the point of tenant scoping. The clean path (mirroring every other tenant-scoped table, all born with surrogate PKs): add surrogate id :binary_id PK, DROP CONSTRAINT secrets_pkey (data-nondestructive — no row or value touched), demote name to a plain NOT NULL column, then the two partial unique indexes. Blast radius: 4 Repo.get(SecretRecord, name) call sites become Repo.get_by, and — unsurveyed subtlety — put/3's upsert (on_conflict conflict_target: :name) BREAKS against partial unique indexes and needs a new conflict-target form. There is NO DROP CONSTRAINT precedent anywhere in the migration history. Verify assignment V1 proves the whole mechanism live before D191 ratifies it; V2 rules on whether per-workspace name reuse is genuinely required (charter + credential_ref semantics say yes, but the ruling must be explicit).

Digest: what else the survey settled

• W6 DEK envelope: NOT reusable — it is connectors/src/crypto/credential-cipher.ts, Node-only, HKDF per-call, deliberately walled off by charter D38 ('no Elixir will ever decrypt one'). The Elixir-native analog, if crypto-binding is ever wanted, is Crypto.DataKeys + FieldCipher (scope-as-AAD, D51-D54). Lean 5 (keep Cloak EncryptedBinary this wave) stands.
• NEW security finding (not previously in the charter): Cloak's AES-GCM AAD is the hardcoded constant "AES256GCM" (deps/cloak aes_gcm.ex:12) — a ciphertext blob copied between rows decrypts cleanly. The W21 tenant wall is SQL-enforced ONLY, never cryptographic. D191 must name this as a residual risk and file the FieldCipher/DataKeys upgrade as an explicit follow-up task — no silent claim of crypto isolation.
• S2 (scoped admin HTTP surface) genuinely requires router.ex lines — the proven :scoped_admin pattern (schemas/webhooks/token-mint, router.ex:2157-2213) needs a new scope block, and router.ex is off-limits this wave. SecretController stays flat-global on the new schema; DANGER noted: the :api pipeline's AssignDefaultScope stamps current_workspace=Default, so the controller must keep calling the GLOBAL tier explicitly, never accidentally scope legacy writes to 'Default'. S2 + the manifest auth_tier flip (bp secret * currently blanket 'admin' in capabilities.ex ~1416-1463) become one named follow-up.
• Knob-4 is NOT a small S3: no grant object exists anywhere (connector_installs has zero permission/scope fields; the mint is hardcoded ~w(read write), auth.ex:678), and W15/D148 already declined the policy half — 'building it would manufacture a fake correlation'. Follow-up filed with the honest amendment: D9 scoping is necessary but NOT sufficient; knob-4 also needs a grant-model design decision.
• No consumer exists today: the Cloud runner deliberately bypasses Barkpark.Secrets (D23/D110 — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from ambient env only). A scoped store lands consumer-less; the wave must say so honestly and file 'wire the first scoped consumer' as a follow-up rather than imply the runner reads it.
• plugin_settings is the same flat shape but a legitimately instance-global sibling (singleton GitHub App / Bokbasen / Indx config) — EXPLICITLY out of scope, named exclusion with a forward pointer, not a leak.
• No naming-convention hack exists (no workspace-prefixed names anywhere); no Studio LiveView renders secrets (nothing to seal there); CLI bp secret * is manifest-driven so sealing HTTP seals the CLI for free.
• Runway is clear: D191 slot free (bp search confirms no rival), task-5766dc5ca985ddc8 unclaimed with zero prior work, no open PR or local diff touches secrets, secrets module last touched 2026-07-01, latest migration on main = 20260716120000.

Coverage map — checked and NOT found (absences are decisions-in-waiting)

• FOUND & settled: secrets.ex / secret_record.ex / secret_audit.ex / encrypted_binary.ex (read in full); create-secrets migration; secret_controller + router pipelines (:require_admin, :scoped_admin); require_ingest_token; content/scope.ex + tenancy.md; chat_sessions seam (migration+store+tests); credential-cipher.ts + rewrap.ts; data_keys/data_key/local_kek/field_cipher; capabilities.ex secret.* manifest entries; plugin_settings trio + all 6 consumers; charter D9/D24/D35/D37/D38/D119/D148/D166/D175/D185/D187-D190; full repo-wide caller census (api/lib, api/test, cloud/, internal/, js/, web/).

• CORNERS NO SCOUT REACHED (verify closes these): connectors/src raw SQL against the Postgres secrets table (grep never run over the TS bridge); BarkparkCloud.Registry.Vault's DEK scheme (only referenced from local_kek.ex moduledoc); the STORED criterion text of task-5766dc5ca985ddc8 / task-fe78ccb664308739 (knob-4 wording — surveys quoted the charter, not the ledger); whether the local targeted mix-test harness actually runs for a fresh worktree (build phase depends on it); the put/3 upsert vs partial-unique-index interaction (nobody tested it); workspaces PK type + FK-vs-no-FK fork (chat_sessions=no FK vs data_keys=FK).

Verify plan — 5 assignments in flight

• V1 migration-and-harness-probe (OPUS, worktree, RUNS): fresh worktree off origin/main. Prove (a) targeted harness: CC=clang mix test test/barkpark/secrets_test.exs green on main; (b) throwaway migration — surrogate id PK via DROP CONSTRAINT secrets_pkey + nullable workspace_id + the two partial unique indexes — runs under MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate; (c) live semantics: same name coexists in ws_a/ws_b/global, dup-global and dup-(ws,name) rejected; (d) the working upsert conflict_target for put/3 against partial indexes; (e) the red-first shape: unscoped get_by leaks ws_a's row to ws_b (RED), where-clause filter stops it (GREEN). CONNECTORS EPIC · WAVE 21 · DESIGN WAVE · STRATEGIZE · 2026-07-17

Wave 21 — Run-secrets grow a tenant wall: per-workspace scoping (D9), designed then built

IN FLIGHT — verifying Survey (12 coverage-accounted reports) is folded in below. A 5-verifier fleet is in flight: 2 Opus (live migration/PK probe in a worktree; PK-fork necessity ruling) + 3 Sonnet (CI gate + collisions, ledger/prior-art, FK + audit shape). Next: Decide ratifies D191+ and cuts slices; builders implement.

The wish

Ratify + build RUN-SECRETS PER-WORKSPACE SCOPING (task-5766dc5ca985ddc8), the D9 premise correction. Today's run-secrets store is FLAT INSTANCE-GLOBAL: table `secrets` with PK :name, columns value/updated_at/updated_by, zero tenant column; Barkpark.Secrets.get/put/reveal/delete key only on name; list/0 returns every secret in the instance; /v1/secrets/* is gated flat :require_admin. This blocks knob-4 (grant-scoped per-workspace token mint, D24) and true per-workspace credential isolation in the Cloud runner. Wave shape: (A) RATIFY the scoping design as a real charter decision D191+, grounded in the actual code + docs/contracts/tenancy.md + the chat_sessions owner_workspace_id prior art, naming the failure mode each choice prevents; (B) BUILD it — schema change + safe migration + scoped read/write + a RED-FIRST protective test proving cross-workspace isolation (must red on today's flat-global code). All offline Elixir, rides elixir.yml. Scope tightly: one coherent capability, 2-3 disjoint slices; knob-4 only if honestly small, else a now-unblocked follow-up.

Premise check (done at Strategize)

Confirmed against origin/main: api/lib/barkpark/secrets.ex + secrets/secret_record.ex are exactly as D9 recorded — @primary_key {:name, :string}, no workspace_id anywhere, Repo.get(SecretRecord, name) on every path, list/0 unfiltered. The D9 premise stands; no contradiction found. One crucial wrinkle the design MUST honor: ingest_token/0 is a legitimate INSTANCE-GLOBAL consumer (DB-first, env-fallback resolver for the cloud ingest shared secret) — a hard tenant seal that abolishes global secrets would break it. The store therefore needs TWO tiers, not a blanket migration of every row into a workspace.

Strategic direction

The finished experience: a workspace's secrets live inside its tenant wall. Workspace A's admin can put/get/list/reveal/delete A's secrets and can NEVER see that B's secrets even exist; a nil or undecidable workspace resolves to ZERO rows (fail-closed, the scope_to_workspace/3 law); instance-global system secrets (ingest token) keep working untouched on an EXPLICITLY-global path that no workspace-scoped call can reach by accident. The knob-4 token mint can then read its per-workspace material without an admin token — the exact anti-pattern D37 called out dies here.

  • Tentative lean 1 — ADDITIVE nullable workspace column, not a PK rewrite of doom. Add workspace_id (:binary_id, nullable) to secrets; NULL = instance-global system secret. Replace PK-on-name uniqueness with two partial unique indexes: UNIQUE(name) WHERE workspace_id IS NULL and UNIQUE(workspace_id, name) WHERE workspace_id IS NOT NULL. Failure mode prevented: a destructive PK migration that could drop or collide existing prod secrets (migrations are irreversible-sensitive; nullable-add + no backfill = zero-risk).
  • Tentative lean 2 — TWO EXPLICIT TIERS, no silent fallback. Scoped reads (get/list/reveal with workspace_id) see ONLY that workspace's rows — a NULL-owner global secret is INVISIBLE to the scoped path, and a foreign workspace's row is invisible. The legacy get/1 global path reads ONLY WHERE workspace_id IS NULL. Failure modes prevented: (a) instance credentials leaking to tenants via fallback-to-global reads; (b) a tenant secret shadowing a system secret name; (c) the D35-class NULL-owner leak where global callers read everything.
  • Tentative lean 3 — fail-closed on nil. A scoped call with nil/invalid workspace_id compiles to zero rows or raises — never falls through to the global tier (mirror scope_to_workspace/3's where:false law).
  • Tentative lean 4 — migration = nullable add + indexes ONLY; existing rows stay NULL (they ARE instance-global today — backfilling them into a workspace would be inventing tenancy that never existed). No dual-read bridge needed because the tiers are disjoint by definition.
  • Tentative lean 5 — keep Cloak EncryptedBinary for at-rest encryption THIS wave; the W6 per-workspace DEK envelope question (does a row-swap attack matter when the value column carries no AAD binding to workspace_id?) gets a survey + verify answer and, if real, a NAMED residual-risk note or a small AAD follow-up — not silent scope creep.
  • Tentative lean 6 — audit rows (SecretAudit) gain the workspace dimension so a reveal in workspace A is attributable to A.
  • Tentative lean 7 — slices: S1 schema+migration+scoped context functions+red-first isolation test (the core, must land); S2 HTTP/admin surface scoping IF it lands without touching router.ex (survey decides; router.ex is off-limits this wave); S3 knob-4 consumer ONLY if honestly small — else file it as the now-unblocked follow-up.

Quality bar: the isolation test MUST red on today's flat-global code before the fix greens it (distrust vacuous green). Column naming follows the repo's own vocabulary — survey decides between workspace_id (tenancy tables) and owner_workspace_id (chat_sessions P0 pattern). Do NOT overreach into the other design gates; keep production diffs minimal.

Survey plan — 14 scouts

  1. secrets-impl-map — Full map of Barkpark.Secrets + SecretRecord + SecretAudit + EncryptedBinary: every public function, changesets, audit shape, the ingest_token resolver. WHY: The design patches THIS code; the ratified D191 must name real functions, not imagined ones.

  3. secrets-http-surface — The /v1/secrets controller + pipeline: how is it gated, does workspace resolution already ride the plug chain, can scoped gating land WITHOUT touching router.ex? WHY: Determines whether slice S2 is in-scope this wave or a follow-up.
  4. tenancy-scope-prior-art — scope_to_workspace/3 in content/scope.ex + the chat_sessions owner_workspace_id P0 slice: exact column shape (nullable? FK? default?), migration text, how the isolation tests were written red-first. WHY: The ratified design copies a proven pattern instead of inventing one.
  5. dek-envelope-w6 — The per-workspace DEK envelope shipped for connector-install credentials (W6): where does it live, what API, does run-secrets reuse it cheaply or is Cloak EncryptedBinary the honest answer this wave? WHY: Settles lean 5 — reuse vs keep, with cost named.
  6. encrypted-binary-aad — Does Cloak/EncryptedBinary bind any AAD/context? Can a ciphertext row be re-pointed to another workspace row (swap attack)? Compare FieldCipher's scope-is-the-AAD scheme. WHY: Names the residual risk or upgrades it to a slice.
  7. migration-shape — Current secrets table DDL (original migration) + latest migration timestamps on origin/main; feasibility of nullable-add + partial unique indexes vs composite-PK rewrite; Postgres NULL-uniqueness behavior. WHY: The migration must be safe and collision-free; PK :name is the invasive bit to design around.
  8. plugin-settings-sibling — Plugins.Settings (the sibling encrypted-KV): same flat shape? Does this wave's design need to cover it or explicitly exclude it? WHY: Prevents scope creep AND prevents a second flat store from becoming the new leak.
  9. knob4-consumer — The D24 knob-4 grant-scoped token mint: where would it consume workspace secrets, what exists already (Auth.create_token/5, chat_token_controller), is it honestly small once scoping lands? WHY: Decides whether S3 rides this wave or gets filed as the unblocked follow-up.
  10. cloud-runner-reads — How the Cloud runner / assignment runtime reads run-secrets today (env injection? resolver poll?) and which of those reads must become workspace-scoped. WHY: The scoped read path must serve the actual runner consumer, not a hypothetical one.
  11. test-harness — Existing secrets tests + DataCase multi-workspace fixture patterns (create_workspace_with_owner): where does the red-first isolation test live and what fixtures does it need? WHY: Builders get a paved test path; the red-first bar is non-negotiable.
  12. naming-convention-hack — Does ANY code already write workspace-prefixed secret names (e.g. slack_bot_token:<ws>) as a scoping hack? WHY: A convention-hack row would need migration accommodation or explicit kill.

Ledger

Survey digest — what 12 scouts established (Digest phase, 2026-07-17)

D9 is confirmed at every layer, live on origin/main: secrets is a flat instance-global encrypted KV. The name column is the LITERAL Postgres primary key (migration 20260629140000: add :name, :string, primary_key: true), every context function keys on bare name (get:29, reveal:42, put:68, list:98 unfiltered, delete:112), /v1/secrets is gated flat [:api, :require_admin] with zero workspace resolution, and secrets_audit has no workspace dimension either. Exactly TWO production callers exist repo-wide: SecretController (admin HTTP CRUD via list/reveal/put/delete — never get/1) and RequireIngestToken -> ingest_token/0, the SOLE caller of get/1 and a structurally instance-global consumer (the bearer check runs before any workspace is resolvable). Consequence: making get/1 global-tier-only (WHERE workspace_id IS NULL) breaks nothing.

Prior art is nailed and directly crib-able: the chat_sessions owner_workspace_id seam (migration 20260713140000: nullable :binary_id, NO FK, no default, no backfill, partial composite index) + studio_chat.ex scope_sessions/2 — a 3-clause fail-closed gate (:global passthrough / binary equality / anything-else -> where(false)) — plus the red-first isolation test template at studio_chat_test.exs:2298-2431, including the critical sub-case: a NULL-owner global row is INVISIBLE to ANY workspace scope, no is_nil OR-carveout. Content.Scope.scope_to_workspace/3 (content/scope.ex:111-127) and docs/contracts/tenancy.md:52 state the same fail-closed law. Test harness: TenancyFixtures.create_workspace! + the content_get_document_tenant_isolation_test.exs sanity-then-leak-guard structure; a secrets-specific direct-insert fixture must be built alongside (none exists).

CONTRADICTION with the strategic direction — the PK cannot silently survive Lean 1 said 'additive nullable column, NOT a PK rewrite'. The migration-shape scout proved that is only half-available: Postgres PRIMARY KEYs cannot be partial, so as long as name stays the PK, workspace A and workspace B can NEVER both own a secret named openai_api_key — which defeats the point of tenant scoping. The clean path (mirroring every other tenant-scoped table, all born with surrogate PKs): add surrogate id :binary_id PK, DROP CONSTRAINT secrets_pkey (data-nondestructive — no row or value touched), demote name to a plain NOT NULL column, then the two partial unique indexes. Blast radius: 4 Repo.get(SecretRecord, name) call sites become Repo.get_by, and — unsurveyed subtlety — put/3's upsert (on_conflict conflict_target: :name) BREAKS against partial unique indexes and needs a new conflict-target form. There is NO DROP CONSTRAINT precedent anywhere in the migration history. Verify assignment V1 proves the whole mechanism live before D191 ratifies it; V2 rules on whether per-workspace name reuse is genuinely required (charter + credential_ref semantics say yes, but the ruling must be explicit).

Review debrief — the tenant wall holds, and the test proves it

One slice, reviewed as the last hands before merge in a fresh worktree branched off the built commit (deea1129b). OUTCOME — the D9 design gate is closed Run-secrets are no longer flat instance-global. The store now carries a two-tier identity (NULL workspace_id = instance-global, non-NULL = one workspace) behind a fail-closed scope gate that mirrors StudioChat.scope_sessions/2. Workspace A cannot read, reveal, list, or delete workspace B's secret; instance globals never leak into a tenant scope and tenant rows never shadow ingest_token; a nil/invalid scope reads zero rows and refuses writes with {:error, :invalid_scope}. The wall is SQL-only, not cryptographic (Cloak's AAD is a constant) — a named, filed residual (connectors-secrets-aad-binding), not a silent gap.

Grade — A

A. This is the design wave D187 called for, executed cleanly. The hard call (surrogate-PK rewrite over the strategize lean's additive column) was made for the RIGHT reason — a name-PK ships a cross-tenant enumeration oracle — and every mechanism was run-proven at Verify before a line was built. The build honors it precisely: fail-closed everywhere, no OR-is_nil cross-tier carve-out, the upsert 42P10 trap and the 500-vs-409 unique_constraint trap both closed, scope creep refused (router/HTTP/Cloak all left alone with named follow-ups). The RED-first proof is real, not vacuous. What holds it back from A+: the wall is SQL-only by explicit decision (acceptable, filed) so 'per-workspace credential isolation' is not yet cryptographic; the down migration ships unproven (CI runs up only) and deletes scoped rows — documented, low-risk, but a latent edge; and read paths take scope as a raw binary, so a future scoped-admin caller MUST guard request input with Ecto.UUID.cast to avoid the binary_id CastError (no caller does today; noted for the follow-up). None of these are defects in what shipped — they are honestly-named boundaries.
